app.title: llm-launchpad
app.subtitle: Pick a model and launch a GPU instance for it

models.cappedHelp: The selected context length is over this model's max ({{max}}), so the estimate uses the max.
models.tightHelp: Less than 1 GiB of VRAM is left. It may not fit on a real instance, so consider the next type up.
models.selectPrompt: Pick a model from the list to see the VRAM breakdown and the recommended instance type.
models.vramBarLabel: VRAM needed {{required}} GiB of {{total}} GiB on the instance
models.fittingTypes: Instance types that fit (in the order they are picked)
models.estimateNote: Estimates are approximate. They assume Ollama serves one request at a time.

region.heading: Region and model storage for {{model}}
region.loadFailed: Could not load prices or region details: {{error}}
region.moveNotice: {{region}} needs its own model storage (an S3 bucket or EBS volume). Changing the region means putting the model there again, since buckets and volumes belong to one region.
region.notOffered: {{type}} is not available in this region. Pick another region.

storageHelp.s3_cache: Copies the model from S3. If it is not in S3 yet, downloads it and saves it to S3 once ready. Cheapest while stopped
storageHelp.ebs: Attaches an EBS volume that keeps the model. Nothing to download, but loading from the volume is slower and storage costs more
storageHelp.download: Downloads from the Ollama library every time. No storage cost

region.ebsThroughput: (of which {{price}} is the {{throughput}} MiB/s throughput of the {{size}} GiB volume)
region.startupFirstLater: first time about {{first}} min / later about {{later}} min

prerequisite.bucket: There is no bucket in {{region}} yet. Apply terraform/model-store first.
prerequisite.volume: There is no EBS volume in {{region}} yet. Create one with model_volumes in terraform/model-store first.

region.hourlyTotalDetail: {{onDemand}}/hour on-demand. Instance, root volume ({{disk}} GiB) and storage added together
region.note: Prices are estimates from the AWS Price List API and spot price history, and differ from the actual bill. Startup time is from terraform apply until ready, worked out from a measurement ({{source}}).
region.confirmBlocked: Some launch checks did not pass, so you cannot continue.

preflight.heading: Checks before launch
preflight.unknown: Could not check ({{error}}). Launch is not blocked, but apply may fail.
preflight.credentialsFix: In the terminal that started the server, set up aws configure or AWS_PROFILE, check that aws sts get-caller-identity works, then restart the server.
preflight.typeFix: Pick another region, or change the context length in the model list to get another instance type.
preflight.quotaNumbers: limit {{limit}} vCPU, in use {{used}} vCPU, needed {{needed}} vCPU
preflight.quotaNg: Not enough ({{numbers}}). "{{name}}" needs to be raised.
preflight.quotaFix: Request an increase in Service Quotas. Approval can take a few days.
preflight.quotaFixPending: Wait for the request to be approved.
preflight.quotaUseOther: The other purchase option (spot / on-demand) can launch with the current quota.

summary.both: You can go on to launch with spot or on-demand.
summary.spotOnly: You can go on to launch with spot (the on-demand quota is not enough).
summary.onDemandOnly: You can go on to launch with on-demand (the spot quota is not enough).
summary.none: You cannot launch yet. Fix the items above, then check again.

launch.title: Launch with these settings?
launch.lead: Yes writes the settings below to tfvars and runs terraform apply. A GPU instance is created and starts costing money.
launch.vramBreakdown: {{required}} GiB (weights {{weights}} + KV cache {{kv}} + overhead {{overhead}}), {{headroom}} GiB left
launch.blockedByPreflight: not available: the quota is not enough

risk.low: Unlikely to be interrupted (Spot placement score {{score}}/10, {{zone}})
risk.medium: May be interrupted at times (Spot placement score {{score}}/10, {{zone}})
risk.high: Likely to be interrupted or fail to launch (Spot placement score {{score}}/10, {{zone}})

launch.riskUnknown: The spot interruption risk is unknown.
launch.riskNote: This is AWS's estimate and may not match reality. When interrupted, the instance stops and resumes once capacity is back.
launch.idleStop: Stop after this many minutes without requests (0 to never stop)
launch.idleStopInvalid: Use 0 or a whole number from 10 to 1440
launch.maxLifetime: Stop this many hours after launch (0 to never stop)
launch.maxLifetimeInvalid: Use a whole number from 0 to 720
launch.envIdHelp: Use a different name per environment. If an environment with this name exists, it is changed.
launch.envIdInvalid: Use up to 20 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, other than default
launch.disclaimer: Prices are estimates and differ from the actual bill. Data transfer and request charges are not included.

progress.heading: Launch progress
progress.empty: Launch from the Choose a model tab and the progress shows up here.
progress.noRecord: There is no record of launching {{workspace}}.
progress.overdueHelp: It can take longer than the estimate depending on capacity and model size. If it fails, the reason shows up here.

stageHelp.creating: terraform apply is creating the VPC, IAM, GPU instance and so on.
stageHelp.booting: Waiting for the instance to boot and start the bootstrap (user data).
stageHelp.preparing_storage: Copying from S3 or attaching the EBS volume, then starting Ollama.
stageHelp.pulling_model: Pulling the model from the Ollama library. If it is already in S3 or EBS, this only checks it.
stageHelp.verifying: Loading the model into the GPU and checking that it answers a short prompt. Large models take a few minutes.

progress.cacheMiss: The model was not in S3, so it is pulled from the Ollama library (and saved to S3 once the instance is ready).
progress.firstResponse: {{sec}} s to the first response (including loading into the GPU)
progress.estimateNote: The time left is an estimate from a measurement (Tokyo, g4dn.xlarge). While pulling, it uses the actual pull speed.
progress.showTerraform: See the full output in the Terraform tab
progress.instanceLogHelp: The bootstrap log on the instance is {{path}}. Open a shell through SSM to check it.
progress.openShell: Open a shell on the instance
progress.tailLog: Read the bootstrap log (inside the shell)
progress.failedCost: The instance is still running and you keep paying for it. If you cannot fix it, delete the environment.
progress.connectionUnknown: The instance is ready, but the connection details (terraform output) could not be read.
progress.portForward: 1. Start port forwarding (keep it running in another terminal)
progress.portForwardHelp: Forwards the Ollama API (11434) to localhost:11434. Needs the Session Manager plugin.
progress.openaiCurl: Send to the OpenAI-compatible API with curl
progress.openaiPython: Send with the OpenAI Python SDK
progress.openaiPythonHelp: Set base_url up to /v1. api_key can be any string.

environments.heading: Environments
environments.lead: Terraform workspaces that have resources or were launched from this screen. Stopping ends the instance charges, but disks and other resources are still billed.
environments.noTfvars: There is no tfvars file from the launch, so it cannot be deleted from this screen. Pass the variables and run TF_WORKSPACE={{workspace}} terraform destroy.
environments.showTerraform: Show the output in the Terraform tab
environments.destroyRunFailed: terraform destroy failed. Check the output in the Terraform tab and delete it again.
environments.costNote: The estimate is the time since the instance last started, multiplied by the current hourly price (for spot, the price in its AZ). Time while stopped, disks, and data transfer are not included.
environments.leftoversLead: Resources with the project tag (Project=llm-launchpad) that are not in any environment's state. Regions checked: {{regions}}
environments.unchecked: Could not query AWS in {{regions}}, so leftovers there were not checked.
environments.leftoversHelp: Terraform cannot delete these. Delete them in the AWS console or with the AWS CLI. Instances are billed while they run.
environments.destroyLead: terraform destroy deletes the resources in this environment's state ({{n}}). This cannot be undone.
environments.destroyInstance: The GPU instance and its root volume are deleted, along with any data on the instance.
environments.destroyKeeps: The model-store S3 bucket and EBS volumes stay (the next launch can use the models in them).
environments.destroyTfvars: When the delete succeeds, {{path}} is also removed.
environments.destroyType: To confirm, enter the environment ID "{{workspace}}"

terraform.heading: Terraform
terraform.description: Each button runs a command in terraform/ and streams its output here.

commandHelp.version: Show the Terraform and provider versions
commandHelp.init: Install providers and modules (run once first)
commandHelp.plan: Preview what would be created (creates nothing)

terraform.planNeedsVars: plan needs terraform/terraform.tfvars (or the values picked in this UI).
